_about: The video style catalogue: each entry is one complete video style (format, hook, length, picture, motion, captions, sound, opening and close), chosen as one thing before the script is written, so the script, the storyboard and the cut are all made to it and production stops being a run of corrections. Krish, 2026-11-10: "I'd like to strategize up front, holistically and in an interconnected way, based on what actually looks good and works impactfully, and also takes less back-and-forth during production to get to publish." Step 1 of docs/plans/2026-11-10-video-style-system/PLAN.md. Every field points at an existing bank, format, device, track or failure by id (python3 scripts/video_styles.py --check). Nothing here is a taste rule: every krish_verdict is 'untested' until he rates the style, and every playbook_format mapping and every evidence card link marked 'engine guess' waits on his yes. The playbook (docs/research/2026-11-10-short-form-video-playbook.md) is an observation, never taste proof.

playbook_formats.insider-access: Film somewhere the viewer cannot go
playbook_formats.absurd-real-scene: A true situation with a punchline, told in under 30 seconds
playbook_formats.its-about-you: Show viewers what a tool already knows or does to them
playbook_formats.changed-this-week: One dated change to a tool everyone uses, and what it means
playbook_formats.resource-drop: Numbered steps, then comment a keyword for the full guide

styles.name: Proof to camera
styles.pitch: Krish to camera, cutting away to the real evidence on the exact words it proves.
styles.hook: The payoff of the title on his face in the first 5 seconds, with the 3 to 7 word claim on screen (hook playbook: opening, shorts).

sound.big_moment: one sound on the verdict only

styles.opening: His face, mid-argument, on the claim.

krish_words.said: just launch straight in to "I put GrokBot and Muse head to head"

evidence.performance: Every Monday to Friday piece through 19 Oct used this production format (style-references formats.production face-with-proof).

never: No evidence shown inside a hand-held phone (week of 2 Nov postmortem, cause A).
No caption that repeats what he is saying.
gaps: The ve format names devices not yet in config/ve/devices.json: document_zoom, logo_row, quote_pull, call_card.

styles.name: The Ladder: one object, every number on it
styles.pitch: One object carries the whole piece and every sourced number is drawn on a part of it.
styles.hook: The hook on his face first, then the object appears with the first number (recipe opening_and_close).

sound.big_moment: one sound on the big moment only (recipe sound)

styles.opening: His face on the hook, then the object.

krish_words.said: I think this was one of the strongest in terms of the animation style of the job badges etc
The chart makes a boring research report instantly understandable (tapped)

evidence.performance: Mon 2 Nov: narrative 6, production 8 (Scores press). His favourite cut, the Critic's first comparison (config/reference-cuts.json).

never: No figures or icons acting out a sentence (recipe never).
gaps: No ve format file; it exists only as a recipe.

styles.name: Voice over pictures
styles.pitch: His voice over pictures only: each line has the picture that proves it, no face.
styles.hook: First frame shows the payoff object moving; the 3 to 7 word claim on screen (hook playbook: shorts).
styles.opening: The picture of the claim, not his face.

krish_words.said: I like how the visuals support most of the absorption of information and with a powerful voiceover this could be a really nice format for certain topics where appropriate.
Might also be nice to not have my face in absolutely everything and mix up the narrative style a little

gaps: The ve format names devices not yet built: photo_parallax, pen_annotation, document_zoom.

styles.name: The lit explainer
styles.pitch: Concede the sensible view, then explain the real mechanism with one human story, to camera, carefully lit, with kinetic subtitles.
styles.hook: Grant the reasonable view, then the sharp claim inside 15 seconds (concession-open).

krish_words.said: The lighting and talking-head nature of her videos are really good and the subtitle effects are really nice as well.

gaps: No ve format file; lighting is a recording setup, not yet on any capture list.

styles.name: The test on screen
styles.pitch: He tests two or more AI tools on the same real job; screen recordings, a live scoreboard and his verdict each round.
styles.hook: "I put X and Y head to head", first person, the test named in the first sentence.
styles.opening: The two tools side by side, the test stated.

krish_words.said: just launch straight in to "I put GrokBot and Muse head to head"

evidence.performance: Wednesday 21 and Friday 23 Oct tests (style-references formats.production scoreboard-test).

never: No score without the round it belongs to on screen.
gaps: bar_compare is named by the ve format but not built.

styles.name: Two passports
styles.pitch: Drawn passport pages explain where an AI was born and where it lives: one illustrated object carries the argument.
styles.hook: The everyday picture first (a passport), then the AI debate it stands for.

krish_words.said: This was very clear and thought-provoking. The production quality was really good and the script was clear as well.

evidence.performance: Fri 6 Nov scored 8 and 8, the week's best; the reel drew 35 Instagram views (postmortem section 1).

never: No mark drawn in frame pixels over a tilted surface (F41).
gaps: Top score, lowest reach: the cover and first frame are the open question (postmortem cause D).

styles.name: The rule you can use tomorrow
styles.pitch: Three to five numbered steps or a three-question test from his own stack, then one keyword for the full guide.
styles.hook: The outcome as a 3 to 7 word claim with a number, on screen in the first frame.
styles.opening: The finished result on screen, then step one.

krish_words.said: the three-question test is simple enough to actually use (tapped)

evidence.performance: The "What could you hand to AI this week?" utility carousel drew 1,792 Instagram views, about fifty times the week's reels (postmortem section 1). One week is a signal, not a rule.

never: Never promise a guide that is not built (playbook production rule 4).
gaps: The keyword DM route belongs to Growth (docs/GROWTH-HANDOFF.md); this engine makes the asset only.

styles.name: Inside the fleet
styles.pitch: An agent in his own operation doing a real job, filmed on the real screens, with the real number and what broke.
styles.hook: The screen itself, mid-job, with the number: no face first.
styles.opening: The real screen, the agent working.

evidence.performance: The playbook names Insider access his strongest bet; Formula 1 garage access video in that set hit 51.1x (observation, docs/research/2026-11-10-short-form-video-playbook.md).

never: Nothing confidential on screen: truth, rights and confidentiality are hard gates.
gaps: Not yet his words; needs a screen-capture list before recording.

styles.name: The absurd real scene
styles.pitch: One true moment where AI did something ridiculous, set up once and turned once, in under 30 seconds.
styles.hook: The oddly specific true line that sounds random until the turn (random-headline-hook).

krish_words.said: The headline is so random it makes you need to know more (tapped)

evidence.performance: The set's top organic video (two AI agents stuck saying goodbye, 593.7x) was this shape (observation, playbook).

never: Only a true scene; never staged and presented as real.
gaps: No track chosen; needs a real moment from client or fleet work.
